disprovenClaims: CLAIM: 'the phase says match CapturePoint.cs:147's shape exactly, so gate Actor.Die on NetContext.IsOffline' — nearly shipped a server regression. IsOffline is FALSE at the server role too, so the naive reading would have stopped the server scoring kills. Disproven by reading the actual server path: MatchStateMachine.ReportDeath owns _score0/_score1 and ConquestScoreRule.Award reads OwnedPointCount, neither of which touches the engine MatchScoreboard. The gate is correct — but only because of a fact the phase text does not state.

CLAIM (the phase's own, task 3.1): 'delete the hardcoded team: 0 at Player Fps Actor.prefab:757'. Disproven as sufficient: offline, that literal IS the only thing that ever set the local player's team — GameManager.StartGame:88 instantiates the prefab and nothing calls SetTeam on it (grep of all SetTeam callers: Actor.cs:1326 declaration, ActorManager.cs:117 for bots, IronfrontNetBindings.cs:190 for server bodies). Removing it alone would have shipped a grey team-(-1) single-player character. A replacement default was added in FpsActorController.Awake.

CLAIM (the phase's own, task 3.1 hazard list): the ownership table assigns the local-team apply to NetClientLocalCombatDriver. Disproven as directly implementable: Net/Client cannot name Actor — the assembly boundary and check-net-layering.ps1 RULE 6b forbid it, which is why ServerPlayerSlotPool takes a body FACTORY rather than a prefab. The apply lives there as the phase says, but reaches the body through ILocalPlayerRig.

CLAIM: 'edit the prefab through the Editor' (P3 § 3.3). Disproven as the right tool HERE: PrefabUtility.SavePrefabAsset rewrote all 239.6 KB of the file, upgrading legacy Unity-5 serialization to the modern format, for a one-int change. The rule's stated hazard is Editor-assigned fileIDs resolving to null; `team` is a scalar int, so it does not apply. The scalar was edited directly and then READ BACK through the Editor (team=-1, 6 object refs, 0 null), which buys the assurance the rule wanted without the rewrite.

CLAIM: 'RemoteActorRegistry's comment says SpawnActorMessage does not carry a team'. Disproven by ServerTickLoop.AnnounceNewActors, which constructs `new SpawnActorMessage(actor.ActorId, actor.Team, ...)`. The comment was stale; the filter is now applied at spawn as well as per-frame, and the comment corrected.
unverifiedClaims: That a team-1 player now SEES a red body. The colour comes from Actor.SetTeam writing ColorScheme.TeamColor onto skinnedRenderer and skinnedRendererRagdoll — asserted only as far as SetTeam being called with the right value. Nothing here rendered a pixel.
That the score labels hold across a real capture flip. The mechanism (UpdateUi never subscribed on a networked client) is asserted; the end-to-end behaviour against a live S_CAPTURE_POINT is not.
That the live body count is 40 + N. The log line exists and the park is unit-asserted; no live server has printed it.

That the minimap filter behaves correctly against a real snapshot stream. ShouldMarkOnMinimap is asserted as a pure function and ApplyMinimapMarker's both-directions call is asserted by reading, NOT by a test — no fixture drives ApplyMinimapMarker against a fake IMinimapMarkers, so 'a body that stops qualifying loses its icon' rests on inspection rather than on a detector.
missingProof: Criteria 1, 3, 4 and 5 — all four live-run artifacts. No lane-B run was performed in this session.
No offline single-player run was performed. Criterion 2's offline half rests on the IsOffline gates plus LocalTeamApply_NeverRunsOffline, not on a played game.
The RemoveMarker branch of ApplyMinimapMarker has no test, per the fourth unverified claim above.
reachableRegressions: If a future caller reaches NetClientLocalCombatDriver.ApplyLocalTeam from a per-actor path, the G4 exemption added for it silently stops applying its guard rule — the same stated residual risk the two neighbouring exemptions (ScriptedRespawnPressed, FirePressed) already carry, and the exemption comment repeats the instruction to delete rather than widen it.

A released player slot (disconnect) resumes its bot brain and becomes an unannounced, unsnapshotted, still-shooting bot — X-18 holds unclaimed slots out of both. That is the same defect family as D-4 one step later, and it is NOT fixed here: the phase explicitly scopes task 3.4 to 'a pool body is suspended from creation', and IAiDriver.Resume's remark documents the resume as intended. Reported rather than silently widened.

G15 matches the LEXICAL guard, not reachability: a call wrapped in a dead `if (NetContext.IsOffline)` passes, and a call guarded by an equivalent predicate spelled differently fails. Stated in the rule's own remarks.

The minimap now marks nothing until the local team resolves. If TryResolveLocalTeam were ever to stop resolving on a live client, the failure presents as a permanently empty minimap rather than an error — the fail-closed direction was chosen deliberately over showing enemy positions, but it is quiet.
